name: La Quemada
local_geology: Rhyolitic tuff and andesite outcrops with residual clays derived from weathered volcanic parent material.
description: Hilltop centre in the Malpaso Valley with monumental terraces, a ballcourt and a votive pyramid. Its ceramic assemblage is dominated by locally produced buff and red-on-buff wares with volcanic temper.

name: Monte Albán
local_geology: Metamorphic gneiss and schist with alluvial clays from the Atoyac drainage.
description: Zapotec capital on a levelled mountaintop above the Valley of Oaxaca. Long ceramic sequence anchored by grey wares fired in reducing atmospheres.

name: Teotihuacan
local_geology: Volcanic ash, pumice and lacustrine clays of the Basin of Mexico.
description: Planned Classic-period metropolis and the production or redistribution node for Thin Orange ware found across Mesoamerica.

name: Chichén Itzá
local_geology: Karstic limestone with palygorskite (sascab) deposits used as temper and slip.
description: Major Terminal Classic centre in northern Yucatán; assemblages dominated by Sotuta-sphere slate wares.

name: Tikal
local_geology: Cretaceous limestone bedrock; calcite and crystalline calcite temper readily available.
description: Central Petén capital with a deep stratified sequence and a large corpus of Late Classic polychrome serving vessels.

name: Copán
local_geology: Ignimbrite and volcanic ash deposits along the Copán River terraces.
description: Southeastern Maya capital known for Copador polychromes and volcanic-ash-tempered fine wares.

name: Cerro Sechín
local_geology: Granodiorite and quartz-rich fluvial sands of the Casma valley.
description: Initial Period coastal centre famed for carved stone monoliths; utilitarian assemblages are coarse and largely undecorated.

name: Sitio Conte
local_geology: Fine iron-rich alluvial clays of the Río Grande de Coclé floodplain.
description: Elite cemetery on the Río Grande de Coclé; the type site for the Conte polychrome style and a key reference assemblage for central Panama.
